name: Cipollone v. Liggett Group, Inc.
summary: The Supreme Court ruled that federal cigarette labeling laws preempted some but not all state tort claims against tobacco companies, establishing that preemption of state tort law must be based on clear congressional intent.
significance: The Court addressed the scope of federal preemption of state tort claims in the context of cigarette warning labels, offering a framework for analyzing when federal statutes displace state common law remedies.
